title: Labor axes Play School presenter Rhys Muldoon on Peta Credlin comments
text:
By KINTA WALSH-COTTON, SHOWBUSINESS REPORTER, AUSTRALIA and CAITLIN POWELL - NEWS REPORTER

Published:  09:45 AEST, 15 September 2026   |  Updated:  12:34 AEST, 15 September 2026

Former Play School presenter-turned-Labor staffer Rhys Muldoon has lost his job after unearthed tweets revealed he once called Peta Credlin a 'strap on fantasy' and another senator a 'fake jew'.

The 60-year-old joined the world of politics after moving to Tasmania and has been advising first-term Labor Senator Richard Dowling since July.

But he was sacked on Tuesday after his social media posts resurfaced, including a string of tweets directed at Sky News host Peta Credlin which made several sexual references.

'She's what Liberals think of Margaret Thatcher. They picture her with a strap on, pounding away at their sorry a**es,' he said in a post seen by news.com.au.

'The tragedy of Peta Credlin... is her belief that anyone other than fetishised old white men think she contributes anything apart from a compromised boner,' he wrote in another.

Rhys used the N-word in a separate social media post and, in another message, referred to Liberal Senator Jacinta Nampijinpa Price as a 'quisling', a term commonly used to describe a traitor - originating from Vidkun Quisling whose ideology was rooted in Nordic racial superiority.

Rhys Muldoon, 60, was dismissed from his role with Labor Senator Richard Dowling after a series of historic social media posts resurfaced

One such tweet saw the former Play School presenter, who has been advising first-term Labor Senator Richard Dowling since July, use the N-word

Rhys wrote a string of tweets directed at Sky News host Peta Credlin which made several sexual references

He also lashed out at his former House Husbands co-star Tim Campbell on March 26, 2014, calling him a 'n***er jew f*g dog' in a highly offensive public tweet.

Tim appeared to call Rhys a 'homophobe' over another tweet he made, leading to the shocking outburst.

'I am protected under 28a you n***er jew f*g dog smoking liberal voter. X,' Rhys wrote in the 2014 post. It is unclear which section 28a Rhys was referring to.

On Tuesday, Senator Dowling confirmed he had sacked Muldoon over the social media posts.

'After being alerted to abhorrent tweets from my staffer, I've decided to not continue with his casual contract,' he told the publication.

'Everyone in public life has a responsibility to do better when it comes to political discourse. The words used were unacceptable at any time.'

Credlin told news.com.au Prime Minister Anthony Albanese should take responsibility for his Labor staffers.

'Is violent, sexual name-calling really the standard that the Prime Minister now accepts in his staffing ranks?' she said.

Rhys starred on Play School from 2000 to 2012

Other messages showed him criticising Senator Jacinta Nampijinpa Price, including one in which he called her a 'quisling'

Senator Price said the remarks by Rhys were 'repulsive'

Senator Price also took aim at the Prime Minister for giving Muldoon 'a plum gig in his government'.

'Mr Muldoon's remarks are repulsive. They have no place in modern Australia, and Mr Muldoon has no place working for the Australian Government,' she said.

It was only revealed earlier this month that Rhys had been recruited by Dowling as a staffer.

'He understands politics instinctively, writes brilliantly, thinks differently to me and isn't afraid to say it,' Dowling told Politico.

'That's exactly why I wanted to work with him.'

Rhys had long been involved in political and public policy discussions before taking the role.

The actor and writer once collaborated on the children's book Jasper & Abby and the Great Australia Day Kerfuffle with former Prime Minister Kevin Rudd.

He also once penned an essay for The Monthly about the removal of the Australian diplomat from leadership, which was named 'an essay of the year'.
